report_name: EndZone Ransomware Claims Breach of Gov't Software Firm Accela

threat_actors.name: EndZone
threat_actors.description: A newly surfaced ransomware group that claimed responsibility for a cyberattack on Accela, Inc. The group uses double-extortion tactics, threatening to leak exfiltrated data from its victims on a dark web leak site.
threat_actors.goals: To extort a ransom payment from the victim, Accela, Inc., by encrypting their data and threatening to leak sensitive information.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
attack_patterns.description: The EndZone group claimed to have exfiltrated over 50 GB of sensitive data, including PII of government workers and citizens, before deploying the ransomware.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: The EndZone ransomware group encrypted data on Accela's systems to disrupt operations as part of a double-extortion attack.

malware.name: EndZone Ransomware
malware.description: A ransomware used by the EndZone group to encrypt victim files and exfiltrate data for double-extortion purposes. The malware is associated with a file extension like '.endzone' and a ransom note.

identities.name: Accela, Inc.
identities.description: A prominent U.S. provider of cloud-based software for government agencies, targeted by the EndZone ransomware group. The company reportedly had over 50 GB of sensitive data stolen.

identities.name: FBI
identities.description: The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation. Data pertaining to FBI agents was allegedly stolen during the breach of Accela, Inc.

infrastructure.name: EndZone Dark Web Leak Site
infrastructure.description: A dark web site used by the EndZone ransomware group to post claims of their attacks and threaten to leak stolen data.

infrastructure.name: EndZone C2 Server
infrastructure.description: Command and control infrastructure used by EndZone to exfiltrate 50 GB of data from the victim, Accela.

indicators.name: EndZone Ransomware File Extension
indicators.pattern:
title: EndZone Ransomware File Extension
id: 25d8a9e0-b3f1-4c6a-8d7e-9f0a1b2c3d4e
status: experimental
description: Detects files being renamed with the .endzone extension, which is indicative of the EndZone ransomware.
references:
  - https://www.dexpose.io/endzone-ransomware-targets-accela-inc/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-20
tags:
  - attack.t1486
level: critical
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '.endzone'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects files being renamed with the '.endzone' extension, a potential indicator of EndZone ransomware activity.

indicators.name: Ransomware Volume Shadow Copy Deletion
indicators.pattern:
title: Ransomware Volume Shadow Copy Deletion
id: 8c7b6a54-3d2e-4f1a-9b8c-7d6e5f4a3b2c
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a common technique used by ransomware to inhibit system recovery.
references:
  - https://www.dexpose.io/endzone-ransomware-targets-accela-inc/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-20
tags:
  - attack.t1490
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'delete'
      - 'shadows'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of 'vssadmin.exe delete shadows', a common ransomware behavior to prevent system recovery.

indicators.name: Anomalous Large Data Egress
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Large Data Egress
id: 1a2b3c4d-5e6f-4a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
status: experimental
description: Detects unusually large outbound data transfers, which could indicate data exfiltration prior to a ransomware attack.
references:
  - https://www.dexpose.io/endzone-ransomware-targets-accela-inc/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-20
tags:
  - attack.t1041
level: medium
logsource:
  category: firewall
detection:
  selection:
    action: 'allow'
  timeframe: 1h
  condition: selection | count(dst_ip) by src_ip > 50000000000 # Example threshold for 50GB, needs SIEM-specific implementation
indicators.description: Detects large, anomalous outbound data transfers that could be indicative of data exfiltration.
